8493.t: A nominal formation from ταμεῖν (tămeîn, “to cut up; to divide”), active aorist infinitive of τέμνω (témnō, “to cut; to hew”), though the exact morphological details are unclear; by surface analysis, τέμνω (témnō) + -ίας (-ĭ́ās).

8466.t: From Proto-Hellenic *skʰḗmə, from Proto-Indo-European *sǵʰ-éh₁-mn̥, formed from the zero grade of Proto-Indo-European *seǵʰ- (“to hold”), synchronically corresponding to ἔχω (ékhō, “to have”) + -μα (-ma).

8491.t: According to Beekes, probably from Proto-Indo-European *ten- (“stretch”), the same root underlying τείνω (teínō, “to stretch”), though the phonological and morphological details are rather unclear.

8499.t: Possibly related to ταρχύω (tărkhū́ō, “to bury solemnly”)

8451.t: Beekes marks the word's origin as unknown.

8458.t: σφάλλω (sphắllō, “to fall, to be cast down”) + -μα (-mă, suffix forming neuter nouns)

8462.t: By surface analysis, σχίζω (skhĭ́zō) + -τός (-tós). Probably from Proto-Indo-European *skidtós, whence also Latin scissus and Proto-Slavic *čistъ.

8452.t: Generally considered to be from Proto-Indo-European *bʰey- (“bee”). Beekes rejects this in favor of a Pre-Greek origin possibly shared with ψήν (psḗn, “gall-insect”).

8474.t: From σάττω (sáttō, “to cram, to stuff”) and the suffix -μα (-ma). Possibly ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *twenk- (“to press, squeeze”) (Proto-Germanic *þwangiz).

8490.t: The suffix "-ινθος" proves a Pre-Greek origin. The form τερέβινθος (terébinthos) was perhaps influenced by ἐρέβινθος (erébinthos, “chickpea”).

8467.t: According to Beekes, undoubtedly of Pre-Greek origin.

8472.t: There is no certain etymology. The word is similar to σκῦλα (skûla, “booty, spoils”), but their relation is unclear, and Beekes is hesitant to assign the word to Pre-Greek, assuming an interchange in initials of σ-/σκ-.

8459.t: According to Beekes, perhaps of Pre-Greek origin, apparently based on the pre-nasalization of the -γγ- (-ng-) as well as the lack of credible cognates in other Indo-European branches.

8476.t: From συγκαλέω (sŭnkăléō, “to call to council, convoke, convene”) + -τος (-tos). In the Byzantine sense, a semantic loan from Latin senātus.

8439.t: From συν- (sun-, “with”) + τυγχάνω (tunkhánō, “to happen (to), I succeed, I light upon, I obtain”).

8465.t: Probably from a Proto-Indo-European *skeh₂- (“to split”), and generally compared with Sanskrit छ्यति (chyati, “to split, hurt”), from the root छो (cho, “to cut off”).
